text_blocks.snippet: The largest planet in our solar system is Jupiter, a massive gas giant.

list.snippet: Size: Jupiter has a diameter of about 88,846 miles (142,984 km), making it roughly 11 times wider than Earth.
Volume: You could fit more than 1,300 Earths inside Jupiter.
Mass: It is more than 300 times more massive than Earth and outweighs all other planets in the solar system combined by about 2.5 times.
Composition: Like the Sun, it is made almost entirely of hydrogen and helium.
Day and Year: A day on Jupiter lasts only about 10 hours, but one orbit around the Sun takes nearly 12 Earth years.

text_blocks.snippet: If you'd like, I can share more details about Jupiter's moons, its famous Great Red Spot, or compare it to the second-largest planet, Saturn.
